subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: Should per-job and heartbeat elevated exec be solved as a narrow elevated marker, or folded into a broader Gateway-owned scheduling provenance model?
rationale: The remaining work changes host-exec authority, persisted cron schema, heartbeat trust, and upgrade behavior, so automation should not choose the permanent trust model without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Fold Into Provenance Design
options.body: Use this issue as the elevated-exec slice of a broader non-forgeable schedule and execution provenance model, with heartbeat covered explicitly.

options.title: Implement Narrow Elevated Markers
options.body: Add per-job and heartbeat elevated authority fields now, but require explicit create, update, execution audit, and migration semantics.

options.title: Keep Wildcards Temporarily
options.body: Defer implementation and document the current wildcard risk while preserving existing trusted unattended workflows.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Provenance Design
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the elevated-exec slice of a broader non-forgeable schedule and execution provenance model, with heartbeat covered explicitly.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged cron caller-scope work is the closest current security-boundary change in this area.
